author: WalterBloomberg
text: INFLATION TAKES CENTER STAGE AFTER STRONG JOBS REPORT BlackRock’s Jeff Rosenberg says strong August jobs data shifts attention to next week’s CPI report and the Fed’s September rate decision. Payrolls rose 162,000, beating forecasts and pushing Treasury yields higher. Rosenberg expects the Fed to hold rates if inflation keeps easing. The bigger risk is rising energy costs feeding into core inflation. Even a 25-basis-point hike is unlikely to significantly shake stocks or credit markets. ( @WalterBloomberg )

author: WalterBloomberg
text: TRUMP CALLS FOR LOWER RATES AFTER JOBS BEAT President Trump hailed the addition of 162,000 U.S. jobs in August, saying the figure smashed expectations. He urged the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates, arguing America’s stronger economy deserves the world’s lowest rates. Trump also threatened to halt trade with countries running surpluses with the U.S., saying this could pressure trading partners while avoiding tariffs. “High interest rates put the U.S.A. at a very unfair disadvantage,” he said. ( @WalterBloomberg )

author: WalterBloomberg
text: US hiring plans continue to improve: US-based employers announced plans to hire 12,325 workers in August, the strongest August total since 2022. This marks a +725% increase from the 1,494 recorded in August 2025. Aerospace and Defense led all industries, with 4,025 announced hires, followed by Technology at 2,520, and Industrial Goods at 1,856. Year-to-date, US hiring plans surged +37% YoY, to 119,825 workers, the strongest January-to-August total since 2023. Technology leads all sectors with 19,751 announcements so far in 2026, followed by Aerospace and Defense, at 16,541, and Automotive, at 14,937. Meanwhile, manufacturing industries now account for 46% of all announced hiring plans this year. Hiring plans are gaining momentum. ( @TheKobeissiLetter )
